notes: Seven own pages read, all HTTP 200 and not thin (two are info.visageimaging.com landing pages cited by the answers). The page-candidates home field pointed at a KLAS page and was ignored. Help-file PDFs cited by answers were not read (the fetch tool does not extract PDF text). 'Visage 7' is the vendor's index alias, and 'Visage 7 Enterprise Imaging Platform' and 'Visage Thin Client' were treated as name mentions or architecture descriptions. Server-side rendering, thin-client streaming, speed figures, KLAS scores, net-new selection rankings, 'premium-priced' and cost comparisons, the 'patented streaming' line and the Trinity Health deal value were treated as capability descriptions, ratings, comparisons or out-of-scope facts. Answers saying Visage 'requires a third-party archive' or is 'primarily a universal viewer' were treated as capability statements and not coded, although the technical page describes Visage 7 Open Archive as a core component; a reviewer may want them coded. C09 (zero-footprint) is unverifiable: the technical page calls Visage 7 a native smart-client with zero client-side dependencies and a March 2026 release lists Visage 7 Web, neither of which says zero-footprint. No claim is wrong or stale, so no cited page was read for causes. Pass 2 (8 Oct 2026): no browser snapshot exists for Visage and no page was blocked or thin; the other snapshots were searched again for Azure, the five-year cloud share, zero-footprint, a Pro Medicus RIS and a trial, and none settles C05, C06, C09 or C20 to C23, so nothing was re-classed. The 17 gap lines are rankings, capability descriptions, offers of further help, the Trinity Health deal or lines about other vendors, so none was added. The markdown tables, the Google-style pipe tables (which do not start with a bar) and every Visage-headed section were read in full: two cloud-deployment statements were added to C01 (the q6 Claude 3 best-for line and the q5 Google AI Mode 3 table row giving Server-side rendering / Cloud as the deployment model); other table cells repeat claims already listed for the same answer or are ratings, cost comparisons and the GE Healthcare backing comparison. With no wrong or stale claim, the consistency check changed nothing.
